phase: ROADMAP Stage 2B: auditable library search and claim verification panel v1
implemented: Added a real Library search/audit tab in frontend/index.html with libSearchQuery, libSearchAuthority, libSearchSourceType, libSearchRegion, libClaim, searchBtn, verifyClaimBtn, searchMsg, and searchResults.
Fixed the broken frontend wiring where app.js referenced missing search DOM ids and could interrupt Library UI event binding.
Reworked renderSearch to show result count, vector enabled state, BM25 parameters, fused_score, per-channel rank/score, hit_reasons, document metadata, location, and excerpt.

Reworked verifyClaim to show status, reasons, required_markers, missing_markers, coverage_ratio, covered_markers as marker -> chunk-id list, supporting_items, matched_markers, matched_terms, hit_reasons, and cited_chunk_ids.
Added empty query/claim guards so the UI shows a message and does not call the API with blank input.
Kept all server/user-rendered content escaped through escapeHtml and explicitly labels this as lexical coverage, not semantic entailment.

Added stdlib-only tests/test_frontend_ui.py with 9 static assertions covering required DOM ids, renderer functions, surfaced audit fields, no mojibake question-mark runs, lexical/semantic wording, empty-input guards, and escaping.
Updated README, ROADMAP, and RETRIEVAL_EVALUATION docs to record the auditable panel v1.
not_implemented: Semantic entailment and conflict evidence detection remain out of scope for this stage and require later LLM/NLI work.
Vector retrieval, embeddings, vector storage, and semantic reranking are still not implemented.
A real anonymized 50-100 case retrieval/claim verification evaluation set is still not built.
Automated browser interaction is a smoke check only; full visual/accessibility regression coverage is not yet implemented.
test_commands: python -m py_compile backend/server.py tests/test_library.py tests/test_frontend_ui.py tools/evaluate_retrieval.py tools/run_quality_gates.py tests/test_quality_gates.py
Chrome DevTools smoke on http://127.0.0.1:8766/: open app, click Library, click Search/Verify tab, trigger empty search and empty claim guards, inspect console/network
test_status: Codex verified on Windows review repo: py_compile passed; unittest discover ran 97 tests OK; tools/run_quality_gates.py --json returned passed=true with 5 gates passed; git diff --check passed. Chrome DevTools smoke loaded the app, opened the Library panel, opened the Search/Verify tab, confirmed the required controls were visible, and verified the empty-search and empty-claim guard messages. DevTools showed no JavaScript runtime exception; non-blocking browser notices remained: favicon.ico 404 and existing form label/id accessibility issues. Independent rg credential scan found no secret-shaped tokens.
dependencies: Frontend remains native HTML/CSS/JS with no npm, CDN, or external assets.
New tests use Python standard library only.
review_notes: The task intentionally avoids claiming semantic proof. UI copy says lexical coverage is not semantic entailment and still needs human semantic review.
The prior missing-DOM issue is fixed because index.html now defines every id app.js binds for search/verify.
The browser environment injected Kaspersky requests during DevTools testing; these were outside the app code and are not repository dependencies.
Chrome reported form label/id accessibility issues across the broader existing page. They are non-blocking for this feature but should be handled in a later accessibility hardening pass.
risks: Static frontend tests can prove wiring tokens and fields exist, but they cannot replace full DOM behavior and accessibility regression tests.
Search rendering depends on the existing backend response shape for channels, bm25, vector, and hit_reasons.
Lexical overlap can still be false-positive when the same number or year appears in unrelated context.
